A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work by the same authors. All 35 pages of v3 and 33 pages of v4, including Appendices A–C, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v3 reports original dynamic-programming, in-context-learning, and WikiText-103 experiments in Tables 1–3, with additional training/test results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v4 reports original reasoning, in-context-learning, and WikiText-103 experiments in Tables 2–4, including Sudoku and Countdown results and supplementary results in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The theoretical network construction changes from one attention head to two, with hidden dimension 17d+9 and feed-forward width 49d+25 replacing 24d+1 and 99d+8. Appendix A revises the corresponding attention and bit-extraction constructions. The practical timestep-encoding procedure in Section 4.2 remains unchanged.

E1.justification: v4 adds Sudoku and Countdown evaluation and removes Subset Sum and Knapsack experiments. It retains edit distance, longest common subsequence, decision-tree in-context learning, and WikiText-103, while adding an ED(40) condition. This substantially changes reasoning-task coverage.

E2.justification: The empirical comparisons retain standard Transformers, Looped Transformers, and the timestep-encoding variant. Different Transformer depths are configuration changes. v4's new Table 1 compares theoretical literature rather than introducing evaluated empirical baselines.

E3.justification: New protocols include 3M/100K training/test Sudoku examples and 5M/1K Countdown examples, with 10% of target numbers reserved for evaluation. These comparisons use six-layer Transformers and 4–32 loops; LCS evaluation extends to 100 loops. Appendix C.5 also replaces v3's eight-head ICL specification with a generic four-head configuration, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Loop-count analyses extend to 100-loop LCS and the new reasoning tasks. Conversely, WikiText's 1-, 3-, and 6-loop comparison is reduced to six loops. The ED(60) training/test-correlation analysis in Figure 5 is retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experiments. Both present point estimates and unaccompanied training/test curves.

E6.justification: v4 adds substantial results, including 90.2% Sudoku and 90.5% Countdown accuracy with timestep encoding at 32 loops. New LCS(60) results at 100 loops are 96.9% without and 97.1% with encoding, below the respective 50-loop results. Subset Sum, Knapsack, and lower-loop WikiText entries disappear. Retained numerical entries agree up to rounding.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.7 becomes Theorem 3.6 with r>N, an additional (Nd)^(1/p) factor, a weight-magnitude-dependent error term, and a bit-complexity bound. New Appendix A.2 analyzes bounded-weight quantization and softmax approximation. Other appendix constructions, domains, matrices, and dimensional bounds are substantively revised.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain approximation-rate analysis using three continuity moduli, identification of a loop-specific limitation, and timestep-conditioned scaling to address it. The abstract's empirical message and the claimed novelty of studying Looped Transformer function approximation remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly qualifies universality by infinite weight precision. It removes v3's discussion that WikiText test perplexity remains worse than standard Transformers and that the mechanism behind DP success is unclear. The conclusion instead highlights variable-length inputs, lower bounds, and function classes avoiding dimensionality dependence.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds Sudoku/Countdown encoding and generation details and first discloses input-embedding injection at every loop and intermediate-loop supervision for Sudoku and ICL. These disclosures do not establish procedural changes. v4 removes WikiText's block size, gradient-accumulation count, and task-specific optimizer details while consolidating training information.

R1.justification: The introduction and background substantially expand positioning around reasoning limitations, prompting, generalization, and computational resources. New citations include Merrill and Sabharwal, Saunshi et al., and Vardi et al.; several earlier citations disappear. New Table 1 explicitly distinguishes prior theoretical settings and the paper's contribution.

P1.justification: The introduction, background, continuity explanations, proof sketch, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Definitions move between sections, experiments are reorganized into settings and results, and Appendix C consolidates training information. v4 also introduces an impact statement and conference-format author/header text.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a two-column main text and references, adds a theoretical-comparison table, and restructures experimental tables. It removes the timestep-architecture and full proof-overview diagrams, adds contextual-ID and smoothed-step illustrations, and redraws the continuity and quantization figures. Figure 5 retains the same analysis.

improvement.justification: v4 clarifies parts of the construction and broadens reasoning evidence, but removes useful loop comparisons and reproducibility details. Its new bounded-weight proof also relies on an unsupported ordering: Appendix A.2, Eq. 120 asserts gS<gH, although admissible v=(2,1) and a=(-1,1) give gS>gH. These benefits, losses, and unresolved theoretical support prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
